prompt:
Use case: illustration-story. PRODUCTION REFERENCE SHEET, landscape, not a finished book page. Bold clean clear 2D children's cartoon throughout, crisp continuous dark outlines, flat clean colors, restrained smooth cel shading, no painted or grainy texture, no gouache, no embossed relief, no 3D. Original friendly readable illustration. Ordinary neutral settings; no flags, religious/political symbols or costumes. No logos, text, letters, numbers, pseudo-writing, captions, watermarks or page borders. Natural anatomy and coherent hand/prop contact. Essential content at least 8 percent inside every edge.
WD-KIT / Kit: six-year-old human boy, golden light-medium skin, short straight black side-parted hair, teal T-shirt, mustard shorts, navy sneakers. WD-ZOE / Zoe: six-year-old human girl, deep brown skin, black hair in two puffs, yellow T-shirt, plum overalls, white sneakers. Kit and Zoe have equal standing height. Include only characters needed by this exact scene, not every reference pose. Preserve exact reference identity and clothing.
Book: The Saved Cracker; World Discovery; fiction.
Setting: Classroom snack table, two chairs, clean tabletop. Only Kit and Zoe; all food is already prepared.
Design locks for the book's recurring subjects/props (NOT a visibility list; never insert later objects/states prematurely): One small white plate with a blue rim for Zoe; Two identical square crackers: Zoe’s on her plate and Kit’s untouched in his box; One yellow lunch box for Kit; One small piece of cheese on Zoe’s plate; A few crumbs after Kit eats
 Create a clean separated reference board on white: show the principal recurring props/animals in front, side and three-quarter views, their relative scale beside any named human cast, and a single simple location key showing the persistent setting and daylight/palette. The human character model sheet is a supporting identity reference, not content to copy wholesale. Show only the subjects this book requires. Use initial object states: Kit’s identical cracker remains untouched inside his yellow lunch box. Zoe’s cup is not on the table yet.. For orientation, the opening location/action is: Zoe leaves her blue-rimmed plate on the table and reaches toward the cup shelf. One whole square cracker and one piece of cheese sit separately on her plate. Continuity: Kit’s identical cracker remains untouched inside his yellow lunch box. Zoe’s cup is not on the table yet.. Do not show a completed craft or later scene merely because the finished object is listed in design locks. No future story events, no captions.

visualReview.note: Directly viewed complete generated board. Kit/Zoe identities and equal-height lineup match cast; blue-rimmed white plate, yellow lunch box, identical square crackers, small cheese piece and classroom table/shelf are legible in clean outlined flat style. Only opening states are depicted in location poses; each final scene still requires its exact page state.
visualReview.limits: Direct agent image/sequence inspection; not physical classroom observation.
